monitorOff: Server monitor is off for this host
sysCoresThreads: {cores, plural, one {# core} other {# cores}}, {threads, plural, one {# thread} other {# threads}}

@sysCoresThreads.description: Physical cores and logical processors of the server's CPU.

@sysUptimeValue.description: How long the server has been up; time is hours:minutes, as 3:07.

sysInfoTimeout: The server took too long to answer
sysInfoNoShell: The server has no POSIX shell (sh) to run the query
sysInfoOff: The server monitor is turned off for this host, so no system info is read.

@memory.description: Short label beside the memory bar; about 4 characters.

netIfacesMissing: Not on this server: {names}. Showing the busiest interface.
searchHosts: Search name, host, user or notes
noHostsBody: Add a server, or import your connections from FinalShell, Xshell and other clients in the connection manager.
transfersEmpty: No transfers yet. Drop files on the file list to upload them.
replaceBody: {count, plural, one {# item with the same name already exists in {dir}.} other {# items with the same names already exist in {dir}.}}
chooseArchiveUpload: Choose folders to upload as an archive
archiveLinksOutside: {count, plural, one {# link was not created: it points outside the folder} other {# links were not created: they point outside the folder}}
archiveLinksNotAllowed: {count, plural, one {# link was not created: Windows allows links only in Developer Mode or for administrators} other {# links were not created: Windows allows links only in Developer Mode or for administrators}}
archiveWindowsName: {name} is not a valid file name on Windows
archiveNoShell: No SSH connection to run tar over
archiveDamaged: The archive arrived damaged ({error}): the files unpacked from it may be wrong. Download it again.
secretStoredNote: Saved in the system's credential store ({store}), never in hosts.json.
secretMemoryNote: Kept in memory only: enter it again after restarting.
secretsUnavailable: The system's credential store ({store}) is not available: passwords are kept in memory only.
monitorChannelHint: Turn it off for jump hosts that disconnect when another channel opens.
encodingHint: The encoding the server's programs read and write, its locale. If text shows garbled, try GBK, GB18030 or Big5.
terminalNextConnect: Changes apply the next time the host connects.
proxySOCKS5Hint: The proxy looks up the host's name, so it can be a name only the proxy's network knows.
proxyHTTPHint: Uses HTTP CONNECT. The proxy must allow connections to the host's SSH port.
proxyJumpHint: Logs in to another saved connection first and connects to this host from there, like ssh -J. The jump host can have its own proxy or jump host.
proxyUserPlaceholder: Leave empty if the proxy needs none
noJumpHosts: There is no other saved connection to use as the jump host.
jumpHostNote: Its host key, login and password are its own, as when connecting to it.
errJumpLoop: The jump hosts form a loop: {hosts}
errJumpHostMissing: The jump host of {host} was deleted
errProxyAuth: Authentication failed: wrong proxy user or password
errProxyRefused: Connection refused: no proxy on that port
errForwardProhibited: Cannot connect to {addr}: the jump host does not allow TCP forwarding (AllowTcpForwarding)
tunnelsIntro: Ports forwarded through this host's connection. Enabled tunnels start when a session to it connects, and stop when it disconnects.
tunnelsEmpty: No tunnels. Add one to forward a port.
tunnelHintLocal: Programs on this computer connect to the listening port; the server opens the connection to the target.
tunnelHintRemote: Programs on the server connect to the listening port there; this computer opens the connection to the target.
tunnelHintDynamic: Programs on this computer use the port as a SOCKS5 proxy; the server opens the connections they ask for.
tunnelLoopbackNote: Listens on 127.0.0.1: only this computer can connect.
tunnelLoopbackNoteRemote: Listens on the server's 127.0.0.1: only the server itself can connect.
tunnelPublicWarnLocal: Anyone who can reach this computer on this port can use the tunnel, without logging in.
tunnelPublicWarnRemote: Anyone who can reach the server on this port can connect through it to the target. The server must also allow it (GatewayPorts).
targetHostPlaceholderLocal: As the server reaches it, e.g. 127.0.0.1
targetHostPlaceholderRemote: As this computer reaches it, e.g. 127.0.0.1
errListenAddrInvalid: Enter an IP address or a host name
errRemoteListenAddrIP: Enter an IP address, such as 0.0.0.0 or ::, or localhost: a host name would be looked up on this computer, not on the server
errTunnelRemoteHostName: The server listens on an IP address, not the host name in {addr}: change it to an IP address, or localhost
errTunnelDuplicate: Another tunnel already listens on this port
procFilter: Filter by name, command line or user
procCountFiltered: {shown} of {count, plural, one {# process} other {# processes}}
sigKILL: Ends the process at once; it cannot clean up.
sigHUP: Hangs up; many daemons reload their configuration.
sigINT: Interrupts the process, as Ctrl+C does.
sigSTOP: Pauses the process until it gets SIGCONT.
killBody: This sends SIGTERM, which asks the process to quit. If it is still running after {seconds} seconds, you can force it with SIGKILL.
killWaiting: Waiting for the process to quit…
killStillBody: It did not quit after SIGTERM. Force it to quit with SIGKILL? It cannot clean up.
procAlreadyEnded: The process has already ended. No signal was sent.
tunnelsOffline: Tunnels start when the session connects.
errTunnelRemoteDenied: The server did not listen on {addr}: the port is in use there, or forwarding is not allowed
errTunnelUnknown: This version does not support this kind of tunnel
errTunnelLost: Stopped: the connection to the server closed
hostKeyBody: The identity of {host} cannot be verified. Check that this fingerprint matches the server's before trusting it.
errHostKeyChanged: The host key does not match the saved one ({fingerprint}). Someone may be intercepting the connection. If the server was reinstalled, remove its old entry from {file}.
errHostKeyTimeout: Timed out waiting for the host key to be confirmed
errReadKey: Could not read the private key: {error}
errParseKey: Could not parse the private key: {error}
errNeedPassphrase: The private key is protected: enter its passphrase
errWrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase for the private key
errNoAuth: No way to log in: enter a password or a key
errAuthFailed: Authentication failed: wrong user, password or key
errRefused: Connection refused: no SSH service on that port
errTimeout: Connection timed out: check the address, port and network
errNoSuchHost: Host not found: the name does not resolve
lookAppliesNow: Changes apply to every open terminal at once.
fontFamilyHint: Installed monospaced fonts are suggested as you type. Several, separated by commas, are tried in order.
fontLineHeightHint: A multiple of the font's own line height.
fontWeightHint: Bold text is drawn heavier than this.
fontLigaturesHint: Draws pairs such as -> and != as one glyph, in fonts that have ligatures.
themesSource: The color schemes that Ghostty ships, and your own in Ghostty's themes folder.
backgroundOpacityHint: How much of the image shows through the color scheme's background, which keeps text readable.
backgroundCopyNote: Finallyshell keeps a copy of the image in its settings folder, so moving or deleting the original changes nothing. Remove deletes the copy.
errImageFormat: Finallyshell cannot show this file: choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP image.
errImageTooLarge: The image is too large: the limit is {size} and {megapixels} million pixels.
errImageMissing: The background image is missing: choose it again, or remove it.
appearanceNote: System follows your computer's light or dark appearance. The terminal keeps its own color scheme (Terminal › Color scheme).
optionsComingLater: These options are coming in a later version.
optionConfirmCloseNote: Asks only while sessions are connected or connecting.
optionCopyOnSelectNote: Text you select with the mouse is copied to the clipboard.
rightClickCopyOrPaste: Copy if text is selected, else paste
mouseNextConnect: Open sessions pick up a change when they reconnect.
optionOpenLinksNote: Web addresses in the terminal open in the browser. Open sessions pick up a change when they reconnect.
optionWheelLinesWindows: On Windows, 3 means the lines set in the system mouse settings; other values scale from it.
cmdBarControlName: This name has control characters and can't be inserted
cmdBarPickHint: Arrows choose, Enter or Tab inserts
cmdBarNoSFTP: The server's files can't be read: SFTP isn't available.
cmdBarKeyEnter: Sends the line to the shell
cmdBarKeyTab: Completes a path, or the command name in the first word
cmdBarKeyFields: In the history list: picks one word of the command
cmdBarKeyEsc: Closes the list, then goes back to the terminal
cmdBarKeyFocus: Moves the keyboard to the bar and back (Terminal › Shortcuts)
optionShowCommandBar: Show the command bar under the terminal
optionShowCommandBarNote: A line under the terminal for typing commands, as FinalShell's command input box, with completion and history.
optionCmdBarPathsNote: Lists the server's folder for the path being typed, in columns.
optionCmdBarHistoryNote: Lists the commands sent before; the bar keeps those it sends for each host.
optionCmdBarCommandsNote: Lists the commands on the server's PATH for the first word, read once per connection.
optionServerHistoryNote: Adds the commands in ~/.bash_history and ~/.zsh_history to the history picker, read over SFTP once per connection.
clearAllHistoryNote: The history is kept in the history folder of the settings folder, one file per host. The servers' own history files are not changed.
clearAllHistoryTitle: Clear the command history of all hosts?
clearAllHistoryDetail: The commands kept from the command bar are deleted. This can't be undone.
keySequencesNote: Hosts set to "Default" in their connection settings use these. Changes apply the next time a session connects.
confirmQuitBody: {count, plural, one {# session is open. Quitting disconnects it.} other {# sessions are open. Quitting disconnects them.}}
confirmQuitUnsaved: {count, plural, one {# file in the editor has unsaved changes. Quitting discards them.} other {# files in the editor have unsaved changes. Quitting discards them.}}
editorTooLargeBody: The editor reads a file into memory: one over {limit} takes a while to open and edit.
editorBinaryBody: The editor opens text files only.
editorDisconnected: Not connected to {host}. Your changes are kept, and you can save them once the session reconnects.
editorNotUTF8: This file is not valid UTF-8. It may be in GB18030 (or GBK).
editorUnsavedFiles: {count, plural, one {Save the changes to # file?} other {Save the changes to # files?}}
editorUnsavedBody: Your changes are lost if you don't save them.
editorConflictBody: It changed after you opened it. Overwrite it with your text, or reload it from the server? Undo brings your text back after a reload.
updatesManaged: This copy can't update itself where it is installed. If a package manager installed it (the .deb package), update it there, or download the new version from the releases page.
shortcutsNote: New keys for copy and paste, and Option as Alt, apply to sessions connected from now on.
optionAsAltNote: Option+B then sends Esc b, which moves back a word in the shell, instead of typing ∫.
shortcutCaptureDigits: Press a digit with the modifiers to use, as Alt+1.
shortcutPlain: The shell needs this key. Use it with {mods}.
shortcutShellCtrl: The shell needs Ctrl with this key, as Ctrl+C, Ctrl+R and Ctrl+W. Add Shift.
shortcutShellAlt: Alt with this key is Meta in the shell, as Alt+B and Alt+F move by words.
shortcutOption: Option with this key types a character, or is Meta in the shell with Option as Alt.
shortcutAltGr: Ctrl+Alt with this key is AltGr, which types characters on many Windows keyboard layouts.
shortcutConflict: “{action}” uses this key; it will have none.
shortcutTerminalKey: The terminal uses this key too (select all, zoom, scroll, or copy and paste with Insert); the shortcut takes it.
proxyLater: Connecting through a proxy is coming in a later version.
deleteFolderBody: Its connections and folders move to “{parent}”.
deleteFolderBodyTop: Its connections and folders move to the top level.
managerEmpty: No connections yet. Click New connection to add one.
jumpHostInUse: It is the jump host of {hosts}, which cannot connect until it is restored.
jumpHostInUseForever: It is the jump host of {hosts}, which cannot connect without it.

@problemLine.description: A file not imported from, and why.

finalShellNotFound: FinalShell's data folder was not found. Choose the folder FinalShell keeps its data in, the one with a conn folder in it, or a folder exported from FinalShell.
xshellNotFound: Xshell's sessions were not found. Choose the Sessions folder Xshell keeps them in, under Documents\NetSarang Computer, or a folder with .xsh session files or an .xts export in it.
secureCRTNotFound: SecureCRT's config folder was not found. Choose the folder SecureCRT keeps its settings in, the one with a Sessions folder in it (SecureCRT shows it in Options › Global Options › General › Configuration Paths), or its Sessions folder.
mobaXtermNotFound: MobaXterm.ini was not found. Choose MobaXterm.ini (in %APPDATA%\MobaXterm for the installed version, next to MobaXterm.exe for the portable one), or a file of sessions exported from MobaXterm (.mxtsessions or .moba).
importPasswordsNote: Passwords are not imported, as {source} encrypts them: each is asked for at the first connection.
importNeedsKey: Choose the key file after importing
problemTooLarge: too large for a connection file
problemTooManyFiles: too many files: this one and those after it were not read
importResult: Imported {imported, plural, one {# connection} other {# connections}}, skipped {skipped}, failed {failed}.
importKeysNote: {count, plural, one {# uses a private key: edit it to choose the key file.} other {# use a private key: edit them to choose the key files.}}
importSSHConfigNotFound: {path} was not found. Choose an SSH config file, OpenSSH's client configuration with Host lines.
importSSHConfigNote: An SSH config has no passwords: each is asked for at the first connection. Hosts with an IdentityFile log in with that key.
problemSSHPatterns: patterns only, not a host: its settings go to the hosts it matches
problemSSHPort: the port is not a number from 1 to 65535
problemSSHIncludeLimit: Include goes past 16 levels or 256 files, not read
chooseTableFile: Choose a server list (CSV or Excel)
tableNotFound: Choose a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file with a header row. Only a Host column is needed; Name, Port, User, Password, Private key, Folder and Notes are read too. “Save template…” writes an example to fill in.
tableNote: Passwords in the list go into the system keychain, not into the connections file.

@templateSaved.description: The server list template was saved to path.

@tableColName.description: A header of the server list template; must be one the import reads (importer.ColumnOf).

tableExampleNotes: Replace this row with your servers
tableNoHostColumn: This list has no Host column. Its headers are: {headers}. Name the column of addresses Host, IP or Address (or 主机, 地址, IP地址).
tableWorkbook: This file can't be read. In Excel, save it as an Excel workbook (.xlsx) without a password, or as CSV UTF-8, and choose it again.
tableTooLarge: The file is too large for a server list (at most 10 MB).
problemBadPort: the port is not from 1 to 65535
problemTooManyRows: this row and those below not read: a list has at most 10,000
transfersUnderWay: {count, plural, one {# transfer in progress} other {# transfers in progress}}
downloadFolderNote: Download saves files here. Download to… in the file list's menu chooses another folder for once.
optionAskDownloadDir: Ask where to save each download
fileIconsDetected: Installed in VS Code and similar editors
fileIconsMinimalNote: One icon for files, one for folders
fileIconsNote: Lists the icon themes installed in VS Code, VS Code Insiders, VSCodium, Cursor and Windsurf. A theme installed from a VSIX file is copied into the settings folder. Only the theme's icons are read; nothing in the extension runs.
removeIconThemeDetail: Its VSIX file is deleted from the settings folder.
iconThemeMissing: The chosen icon theme is not installed any more: showing Material Icon Theme.
iconThemeUnreadable: The chosen icon theme could not be read ({error}): showing Material Icon Theme.
vsixNotPackage: This file is not a VSIX package.
vsixNoIconTheme: This extension has no file icon theme.
vsixTooLarge: The VSIX package is larger than 50 MB.
changePermissionsFilesTitle: {count, plural, one {Change permissions of # item} other {Change permissions of # items}}
badFileMode: Enter a mode such as 755: three or four octal digits.
deleteFilesBody: {count, plural, one {It is deleted on the server. This can't be undone.} other {They are deleted on the server. This can't be undone.}}
deleteFoldersBody: {count, plural, one {It is deleted on the server with everything in it. This can't be undone.} other {They are deleted on the server, folders with everything in them. This can't be undone.}}
syncIntro: Keep connections and settings the same on your computers, through storage you already have. Everything is encrypted on this computer with your sync password before it leaves; Finallyshell runs no server and sees nothing.
syncGistTokenHint: A GitHub personal access token with the gist scope. The file goes in a secret gist of your account.
syncGistIDHint: Leave it empty: the first sync finds the gist by its file name, or creates one.
syncWebDAVPasswordHint: Use an app password where the service has them, as Jianguoyun and Nextcloud do.
syncS3EndpointHint: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, AWS S3 or another S3-compatible service. For R2, set the region to auto.
syncPasswordHint: Encrypts what is synced. Use the same one on each computer. It cannot be recovered: if you forget it, replace the remote with this computer's data and a new one.
syncIncludePasswordsHint: The passwords and key passphrases kept in the system's credential store, encrypted with the rest. Private key files are not synced.
syncAutomaticallyHint: At start, a minute after changes here, and at this interval for changes made elsewhere.
syncIncomplete: Fill in every field and the sync password to sync.
syncConflicts: {count, plural, one {# item changed on both sides, this computer's kept} other {# items changed on both sides, this computer's kept}}
syncReplaceRemote: Replace the Remote with This Computer's Data…
syncReplaceRemoteConfirm: The remote file is replaced with this computer's connections and settings, encrypted with the sync password above. What only other computers have is lost from it, and they need the new password.
syncErrWrongPassword: The sync password does not match the one the remote file was encrypted with.
syncErrAuth: The service refused the credentials. Check the token, user, password or keys.
syncErrNotEnvelope: The remote file is not a Finallyshell sync file.
syncErrNewerFormat: The remote file was written by a newer version of Finallyshell. Update to sync.
syncErrTimeout: The service did not answer in time.
netFilter: Filter by name, PID, port or IP
netCountFiltered: {shown} of {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}
netNeedsRoot: Needs root for other users' processes
netConnCountLimited: {shown} of {count, plural, one {# connection} other {# connections}} shown
nextTraceMissing: NextTrace is not on the server. To install it:
nextTraceMissingFallback: NextTrace is not on the server, so {tool} traced the route. To install it:
traceNoTool: None of NextTrace, traceroute and tracepath is on the server.
traceInvalid: Enter an IP address or a host name.
geoAskV4: Show where IP addresses are? This downloads about {size} of location data (ip2region).
geoAskV6: Show where IPv6 addresses are too? This downloads about {size} more (ip2region).
geoDownloadFailed: Could not download the location data: {error}
geoChecksum: the file is not the one expected (its checksum does not match)
geoCredit: IP location data: ip2region (https://github.com/lionsoul2014/ip2region), Apache-2.0 license.
geoDeleteDetail: The ip2region files and the cache of online lookups are deleted, and IP locations are turned off. They can be downloaded again.
optionShowLocations: Show IP locations (downloads ip2region data, about {size})
optionShowLocationsNote: The connections in the Network tab show the country, region, city and ISP of each address. The data is downloaded once into the app's config folder and checked against the checksum the app keeps. Until it is downloaded, the tab shows addresses only and nothing is looked up.
optionGeoOnlineNote: Addresses the downloaded data has no city or ISP for are sent to ip-api.com, a third party (to ip.sb while ip-api.com is busy). The free ip-api.com service is unencrypted (HTTP) and for non-commercial use only. Answers are kept for 30 days; private and LAN addresses are never sent.
optionTraceNote: Trace Route runs NextTrace on the server (nexttrace --json), which locates the hops with its own service. When NextTrace is not installed, traceroute or tracepath is used, with the downloaded location data. The app never installs anything on the server.
